skill.description: Apply the SPARC development methodology across specification, architecture, test-driven refinement, review, and completion with Claude Flow orchestration.
skill.summary: Structure software delivery with SPARC phases, specialized modes, test-driven workflows, and multi-agent coordination.
skill.author: ruvnet

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks and fenced examples. Eight command blocks are confirmed because they invoke Claude Flow through unpinned npx or a local binary. No prompt injection or malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: Npx examples execute an unpinned package or the moving alpha tag.
remediation.suggestion: Pin an exact trusted Claude Flow version, document integrity verification, and require user approval before package execution.

remediation.issue: CLI examples can cause agents to launch external processes.
remediation.suggestion: Label each command as optional and require users to review substituted arguments before execution.

content.value_statement: Complex software work often lacks a consistent path from requirements to completion. This skill applies SPARC phases, specialized modes, and coordinated development workflows.
actual_capabilities: Organizes work across specification, architecture, refinement, review, and completion phases.
Describes 17 specialized modes for orchestration, development, analysis, design, testing, documentation, and memory.
Provides test-driven workflows using the red, green, and refactor cycle.
Explains hierarchical, mesh, sequential, parallel, and adaptive coordination patterns.
Shows Claude Flow MCP and CLI activation methods for common development tasks.
Includes workflows for features, bug investigation, performance work, research, and legacy refactoring.
limitations: The skill provides methodology and examples, not an executable SPARC implementation.
Claude Flow MCP tools or CLI software must be installed and trusted separately.
Performance claims are stated without supporting evidence inside the skill.
Examples require adaptation to the project, tool versions, permissions, and testing standards.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Feature
use_cases.description: Turn a feature request into requirements, architecture, implementation steps, tests, review criteria, and completion checks.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Parallel Delivery
use_cases.description: Divide a complex project among specialized agents while tracking dependencies, shared decisions, progress, and final integration.

use_cases.title: Refactor Legacy Software
use_cases.description: Analyze dependencies, establish regression tests, plan incremental changes, implement improvements, and verify behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Define a SPARC Specification
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a SPARC specification for [feature]. Identify users, requirements, constraints, risks, assumptions, acceptance criteria, and unresolved questions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when a feature idea needs a clear starting specification.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Test-Driven Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan [feature] with a red, green, and refactor workflow. Include test cases, minimal implementation steps, edge cases, and completion criteria.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before implementing a bounded feature with test-driven development.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Architecture Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design the architecture for [system]. Define components, interfaces, data flow, failure handling, security controls, deployment needs, and parallel work streams.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when a system needs architecture decisions and coordinated implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Orchestrate a Complete SPARC Delivery
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an end-to-end SPARC workflow for [project]. Assign specialized roles, dependencies, shared memory, quality gates, reviews, monitoring, and recovery steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for advanced multi-agent planning across the full delivery lifecycle.

output_examples.input: Plan a password reset feature using SPARC.
output: Specification: Define identity checks, token lifetime, rate limits, audit requirements, and acceptance criteria.
Architecture: Separate request, token validation, notification, and password update responsibilities.
Refinement: Write failure tests first, implement minimal behavior, then refactor.
Completion: Review security, run integration tests, document operations, and verify monitoring.

output_examples.input: Create a parallel workflow for an API migration.
output: Architecture role: Define compatibility boundaries and the target contract.
Implementation roles: Update independent services after shared interfaces are approved.
Testing role: Build contract and regression coverage before traffic migration.
Coordinator role: Track dependencies, decisions, rollout gates, and rollback readiness.

output_examples.input: Plan a safe legacy module refactor.
output: Analyze dependencies and record current behavior.
Create regression tests around critical paths and known defects.
Refactor in small units while maintaining passing tests.
Review performance, security, documentation, and deployment impact.

best_practices: Define measurable requirements and acceptance criteria before assigning implementation work.
Store shared decisions and interfaces so every role uses the same current context.
Use tests, security review, performance checks, and documentation as explicit completion gates.
anti_patterns: Do not start parallel implementation before dependencies and interfaces are defined.
Do not treat generated plans, code, or reviews as verified without project-specific testing.
Do not run CLI examples or install packages without reviewing versions, permissions, and arguments.

faq.question: What does SPARC mean?
faq.answer: SPARC covers specification, pseudocode, architecture, refinement, and completion. This skill also includes a separate review phase.

faq.question: Does this skill write code?
faq.answer: It guides coding workflows and describes a coder mode. Actual code generation depends on the connected AI tools and project access.

faq.question: Is Claude Flow required?
faq.answer: The methodology can guide planning alone. The documented orchestration, memory, hooks, and specialized modes require compatible Claude Flow tools.

faq.question: Can I use it without multiple agents?
faq.answer: Yes. Apply the phases sequentially with one assistant, while preserving requirements, decisions, tests, reviews, and completion checks.

faq.question: Does it guarantee 90 percent test coverage?
faq.answer: No. The skill recommends that target, but achieved coverage depends on the repository, test design, tooling, and execution.

faq.question: Are the CLI commands safe to run automatically?
faq.answer: No. Review package versions, command arguments, permissions, and repository state before executing any Claude Flow command.
